sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression confirmed by live-cell anti-FLAG staining of non-permeabilized cells; channel trafficking to the plasma membrane was not disrupted. Electrophysiological function of the FLAG-tagged construct is not explicitly reported in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly names residues 307 and 308 as the junction in a full-length, membrane-anchored KV1.5 construct. Python lookup confirms residue 307 = P and residue 308 = S, both within the authoritative S1–S2 extracellular loop (270–322). The insertion sits 38 residues from the S1 TM boundary and 15 residues from the S2 TM boundary, satisfying the ≥3-residue clearance rule on both sides. The FLAG tag (8 aa) is shorter than the 13–23 aa ALFA-tag target but establishes that this loop tolerates an insertion at this exact junction. Full-length KV1.5 in a KVβ1.3–IRES–KV1.5 bicistronic construct; FLAG epitope inserted between residues 307 and 308 of the S1–S2 extracellular loop by overlapping PCR. The tagged channel was expressed in mammalian cells and used for surface-trafficking studies.

sources.claim: Another construction tagged with a FLAG sequence into the S1–S2 external loop of the K V 1.5 (between residues 307 and 308) of the K V β1.3–IRES–K V 1.5 cDNA was obtained by the overlapping PCR technique ( Table 1 ) previously described [ 43 ].

literature_notes: L2 (HA tag, KVβ1.3–IRES–KV1.5–HA) was evaluated but does not qualify: the clip describes a restriction-enzyme (BlpI/AflII) cDNA swap with no residue position stated, making it impossible to pin insert_after_residue or confirm the tag is extracellular. The conventional 'KV1.5-HA' naming suggests a C-terminal tag, which would be intracellular (residues 516–613), but this is inference, not evidence. L3 (PMC185199) was evaluated but does not qualify: it reports an antibody that recognises an extracellular epitope in the S1–S2 linker of Kv1.5 on live, non-permeabilised cells. Per the rules, antibody epitope mapping — where an antibody binds — is not evidence of where a tag was inserted, and L3 is therefore excluded. No other ledger lines were provided.
